races.name: Larkhall Construction Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Abando
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with German Derby form but completely out of sorts for current trainer, needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Ex-German; five starts in Britain; gelded before fourth on Wednesday on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-German, beaten less than 10l in the German Derby last year; nowhere near that form in two starts for Marco Botti and similar story on his three outings for this yard; gelded before his front-running fourth of ten at Nottingham (1m2f) on Wednesday on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Curran
runners_data.note: Sole front runner whose wind surgery and stable debut suggest current trainer struggling, but tactical advantage is enormous
runners_data.comment: Had wind op prior to his stable debut when he was tailed off at Newbury three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins when trained by Charlie Johnston; sold to join current yard for 6,000gns last October; had wind surgery prior to his stable debut when he was tailed off at Newbury (1m4f, good) three weeks ago; stepping back up in trip will be more suitable but difficult to fancy at present.

runners_data.name: No More Bolero
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course-and-distance win in April, ideally positioned to track Curran and strike late
runners_data.comment: Won here in April off 4lb lower; second at Ripon subsequently but finished last since
runners_data.spotlight: Scored over hurdles last November and recorded his first win on the Flat in Britain, at this track (2m1f, good to firm) in April off 4lb lower; good second at Ripon subsequently but finished last of six back there (2m, good) after slipping on the bend on the first circuit last month; swaps a visor for blinkers and may be worth forgiving latest run.

runners_data.name: Taritino
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 236-day break but won this equivalent race making all two years ago
runners_data.comment: Won this equivalent race two years ago when making all; must come into consideration
runners_data.spotlight: Has won twice over hurdles since his last run on the Flat last October; won this equivalent race two years ago when making all; must come into consideration.

runners_data.name: Percy Jones
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who is 0-22 on turf and beaten 24 lengths last time, hard to recommend on grass
runners_data.comment: 0-22 on turf and beaten 24l on reappearance at Newbury three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins on AW at Wolverhampton; 0-22 on turf and beaten 24l on reappearance at Newbury (1m4f, good) three weeks ago; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Kotari
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on career-low mark but finished last as favourite at Salisbury, form figures suggest decline
runners_data.comment: Last of six on return to action at Salisbury last month when favourite
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't won since recording a three-timer in 2024; last of six on return to action at Salisbury (1m4f, good) last month when favourite; has dropped to a career-low mark and first-time visor goes on; may be worth another chance.

runners_data.name: Golden Garden
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose sole win came on all-weather, disappointing fourth at Goodwood suggests limited ability
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Goodwood last month and finished last of six subsequently at Yarmouth
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came on AW at Wolverhampton last September when trained by Jamie Osborne; flattered by his finishing position when fourth of ten at Goodwood (1m6f, good) last month and finished last of six subsequently at Yarmouth (1m6f, good); cheekpieces are introduced for the first time and needs more.

runners_data.name: Lusaka
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two course-and-distance wins but 5lb better off with No More Bolero since April defeat
runners_data.spotlight: His six wins include two over C&D; no match for No More Bolero when second here (2m1f, good to firm) in April, although he is 5lb better off with that rival; fourth of 12 at Ascot (2m, good) four weeks ago and holds place claims.

races.paceDynamic: Curran is the sole confirmed front runner and will likely dictate from flagfall, with No More Bolero tracking prominently in second. With six hold-up horses behind them, Curran can roll along at a sustainable gallop without early pressure, potentially setting up a situation where the leaders aren't softened up sufficiently. The lack of pace pressure in the early stages means prominent runners like No More Bolero can sit in ideal position, while the large pack of hold-up horses will face a traffic-laden finish. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable late scramble.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Curran gets an easy lead without being challenged early
scenarios.body: The front runner can dictate fractions and kick clear when the field comes under pressure, while the hold-up brigade gets caught in traffic. Curran's style perfectly suits controlling the race from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If No More Bolero sits perfectly behind Curran and pounces late
scenarios.body: The prominent runner gets the perfect trip tracking the leader before moving smoothly past in the final furlong. This course-and-distance winner can exploit the ideal tactical position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and one closer times their run perfectly
scenarios.body: A patient ride from off the pace can work if the early tempo is crawling and allows time to weave through the pack. Taritino's proven stamina could be decisive in a slowly-run staying test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Curran stops completely and No More Bolero also weakens
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish between tired leaders and hold-up horses who left their runs too late. This creates chaos where any of the closers could emerge from the melee.

watchPoints.text: Curran's wind surgery and stable debut tail-end finish raise serious fitness concerns despite tactical advantage
No More Bolero's prominent style could be negated if he gets too keen tracking the uncontested leader
Taritino returning after 236 days but has won twice over hurdles since last flat run
Percy Jones has never won on turf in 22 attempts and was well beaten on reappearance
Track the early pace as Curran may go too slow or too fast without pressure from other front runners

runners_data.spotlight: Always behind after being slowly away when beating only one home on his debut at Newmarket (6f, good) three weeks ago; has been gelded since and drops back in trip; may have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Taseem

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett

runners_data.name: Invincible Isaac

runners_data.comment: Best run when fourth on second start at Nottingham in April.
runners_data.spotlight: Best run when fourth of five on second start at Nottingham (5f, good) in April; has been gelded since his last run and cheekpieces are now added; may do better when switched to nurseries.

races.paceDynamic: Bill The Bull will be the sole confirmed pace-setter in this maiden field, giving him an uncontested lead through the early stages at a sustainable gallop. With no other natural front-runners to pressure him, the pace is likely to be steady rather than fierce, allowing Bill The Bull to dictate terms from the front. The race will develop into a tactical affair where horses need to position well behind the leader, with the real action beginning in the final two furlongs when the field starts to close. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and the lone front-runner, as they will have positional advantages without facing early pace pressure that could compromise their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Bill The Bull maintains his sustainable pace without serious pressure until the final furlong.
scenarios.body: His superior race fitness and tactical advantage from the front proves decisive as the newcomers and exposed horses behind cannot mount a strong enough challenge. The lack of early pace pressure preserves his energy for a strong finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Graceful George can track Bill The Bull in second position and time his challenge perfectly.
scenarios.body: The experienced runner uses his proven ability to sit handy and strike late, benefiting from the steady pace while having enough tactical speed to reel in the leader. His drop back to 5½f with cheekpieces added provides the necessary sharpening.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Newcomer Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the well-bred debutants shows natural early speed to track the leader closely.
scenarios.body: South West or Lucky Larry demonstrates immediate ability to sit prominent and has enough natural talent to quicken past tiring rivals in the final stages. The steady pace set by Bill The Bull suits a horse making a debut who can position well without being asked early questions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Rallies
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes slower than expected and one of the hold-up horses gets a perfect trip through traffic.
scenarios.body: Katie's Cavalier or Invincible Isaac benefits from sitting last, getting a clear run, and having enough finishing speed to make up ground when others have used their energy positioning closer to the pace. The tactical race becomes a sprint finish where pure speed matters most.

watchPoints.text: Bill The Bull could get an easy lead and prove hard to peg back if no horse goes with him early
Lucky Larry and South West are complete unknowns who could show immediate natural ability on debut
Graceful George has tactical speed to sit second and challenge late if the pace becomes steady
Katie's Cavalier dropping back to 5½f after modest 5f debut might not have the pace for this shorter trip
Temple Court and Invincible Isaac both gelded since poor runs and could show improvement with headgear changes

runners_data.name: Stolen

runners_data.comment: Raced too freely and looked awkward ride before dropping out tamely on handicap debut

races.paceDynamic: Geemann stands as the sole confirmed pace-setter but carries fade-in-finish warnings and returns from 248 days off, creating uncertainty about sustained pressure. Forever Glamorous, Gal, Apex Star, Rogue Rebellion and Stolen all show prominent tendencies but several carry similar fade warnings, suggesting the early pace may collapse rather than sustain. With most runners preferring hold-up tactics and the likely pace scenario being moderate early before weakening, this race strongly favours horses that can settle off the pace and deliver late kicks. The abundance of hold-up horses combined with questionable pace reliability creates a tactical setup that benefits patient, finishing types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Geemann sets moderate pace but fades as expected and prominent runners fail to sustain pressure.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish from the back with patient riders able to time their challenges perfectly through a weakening field. Hold-up specialists get ideal positioning to unleash finishing kicks in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Geemann fails to lead effectively and prominent runners are reluctant to commit early.
scenarios.body: The race becomes messy with no clear pace-setter, creating a stop-start rhythm that suits versatile types who can adapt. Horses with tactical speed to move into contention mid-race gain crucial advantages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Early Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners (Forever Glamorous, Apex Star, Rogue Rebellion) all commit to press Geemann from the start.
scenarios.body: The aggressive early pace sets up a true test of stamina over this sprint trip, favouring horses with proven staying power at the distance. Late runners get perfect pace to aim at but need genuine class to reel in survivors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Running Success
scenarios.trigger: If Geemann overcomes his fade warnings and gets an easy lead with soft fractions throughout.
scenarios.body: The returning gelding utilizes his class advantage and natural pace to control proceedings unchallenged. Prominent runners get first crack at the leader while hold-up horses face an impossible task against a horse who doesn't come back.

watchPoints.text: Geemann may fold quickly if pressed early given his extended absence and fade warnings, leaving race without pace
Forever Glamorous and Rogue Rebellion could clash for prominent positions early, potentially compromising both chances
Miss Magic Dragon may get too far back if pace is slow, as hold-up horses need genuine pace to aim at
Gal's betting movement crucial given 212-day absence and stable debut for Mark Loughnane connections
Stolen's settling ability key after racing too freely last time, cheekpieces removal suggests tactical change

races.paceDynamic: Lazzar looks the most likely pace-setter with his prominent style and front-running tendencies, though he's struggled on turf recently and may not sustain strong pressure. The Flying Seagull, Jax Edge, Glamour Show and Tiger Tulip will likely sit prominent positions, creating a decent early gallop over this 5½f sprint trip. With multiple prominent runners and limited confirmed hold-up horses, the pace should be honest but not destructively fast. This race shape favors prominent racers who can track the pace and strike in the final furlong, as pure front-runners may be vulnerable and hold-up horses face a strong gallop to overcome.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Lazzar sets genuine pace but gets caught late
scenarios.body: The honest gallop allows prominent racers to position perfectly and outkick the leader in the final 100 yards. Strike and Lequinto benefit from their hold-up styles if the pace is strong enough to bring them into it late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Lazzar gets an easy lead and kicks clear
scenarios.body: With limited early pressure, the leader gets first run and holds on as prominent horses struggle to make up ground. The lack of genuine early pace plays into front-running tactics.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group goes too fast early
scenarios.body: Strong early pace between multiple prominent runners sets up perfectly for the hold-up specialists. Strike and Lequinto get the perfect scenario with a collapse in front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If favorite prominent runners interfere with each other
scenarios.body: Tactical errors or traffic problems among the market leaders create openings for unconsidered runners. The pace becomes messy rather than tactical.

watchPoints.text: Lazzar may not handle the turf surface as all four wins have come on all-weather tracks
The Flying Seagull often attracts market support but has a history of underperforming when backed
Both Manhattan Mirage and Emporess return from lengthy breaks exceeding 230 days off track
Strike prefers firmer ground conditions and may be inconvenienced by the good going
Multiple prominent runners could create early tactical battles that compromise each other's chances

races.paceDynamic: Dion Baker holds the front-running monopoly and can dictate a sustainable tempo after his Brighton victory, with no genuine pace pressure expected early. Four horses (Wedgewood, Porfin, Rokuni, Coco Hill) want prominent positions creating congestion and traffic problems 2-3 furlongs out on Bath's tight circuit. The hold-up contingent (Jackie Brown, Symbol Of Hope, Magnificent Mel) may struggle to find racing room in the sprint finish. This tactical setup clearly favours the confirmed front-runner who can avoid the squeeze and those who can secure an early prominent position without getting trapped.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dion Baker Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Dion Baker jumps smartly and faces no early pressure from the prominent brigade
scenarios.body: Baker controls the tempo unchallenged and kicks clear when the prominent horses start battling each other in the congested pack behind. His class edge from the Brighton win proves decisive when he gets an uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Royal
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners (Wedgewood/Porfin/Rokuni) press Dion Baker early and create genuine pace
scenarios.body: The increased tempo sets up perfectly for a closer with Wedgewood's course form giving him the edge over the other prominent runners. Jackie Brown or Magnificent Mel could benefit from the strong pace but need significant luck in running.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners create a wall across the track with hold-up horses trapped behind
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with positioning crucial and several runners having legitimate excuses. Whoever gets the clearest run in the final furlong wins by default rather than merit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint from the 2f marker
scenarios.body: A hold-up horse with tactical speed like Symbol Of Hope uses his course knowledge to find the right gap. His Bath record (seven wins here) becomes the deciding factor in a slowly-run tactical affair.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems 2-3 furlongs out when Wedgewood, Porfin, Rokuni and Coco Hill converge in the prominent positions
Monitor how quickly Dion Baker breaks from the stalls as any sluggish start invites pressure from the prominent brigade
Observe Jackie Brown's early positioning as her hold-up style needs the race to develop into a sprint to be competitive
Check if Magnificent Mel can secure a clear run given her 3-year-old inexperience in handling traffic problems
Watch Symbol Of Hope for any signs of his old Bath brilliance returning after two months off the track

races.paceDynamic: Coast will lead unopposed from the gates with Addmann potentially tracking in second early before fading. The single front-runner Coast will dictate comfortable fractions without pressure, creating a sustainable pace that allows the hold-up brigade to close late. With eight hold-up horses including Ken Brulee, Sisters In The Sky, and Spirited Dancer all needing to come from behind, the race sets up perfectly for late closers. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce their best work in the final furlong when Coast begins to tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coast Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Coast maintains sustainable fractions and sees out the trip strongly
scenarios.body: Coast's uncontested lead allows her to kick clear turning for home before the closers can get to her. Her recent better form at Brighton and tactical advantage prove decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Coast's stamina gives way in the final furlong under sustained pressure
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect setup behind honest pace and sweep past a tiring leader late. Ken Brulee's recent win and strong course record for Sisters In The Sky become crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If Coast goes too slowly early and multiple horses challenge simultaneously
scenarios.body: The gentle pace allows too many to stay in contention turning for home, creating a cavalry charge finish. Port Hedland's course form and Little Miss Magic's 5f speed could surprise at bigger odds.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Addmann Shows Early
scenarios.trigger: If Addmann puts pressure on Coast early before predictably weakening
scenarios.body: The rare prominent runner creates faster fractions than expected, setting up the race for closers with the most finishing speed. I Was Thinking's fresh return could be the difference despite turf debut concerns.

watchPoints.text: Coast's early fractions will determine everything - if she goes too fast early, she becomes very vulnerable late
Ken Brulee's jumping from the gates could be crucial given his hold-up style needs the right position early
Sisters In The Sky may need luck in running from her wide draw given her come-from-behind style
Addmann's early position will show if he's improved from the break or remains the same fading type
The pace through the first two furlongs will reveal whether Coast can sustain her advantage to the line

races.paceDynamic: Shirakawa and Elora Prince will likely set the early pace, with Emerald Coast also showing prominent tendencies, but this looks a modest pace given the lack of confirmed front-runners. The majority of this field are hold-up horses who will be looking to come with late runs, creating a potentially messy finish as multiple horses try to find racing room simultaneously. With 11 of the 14 runners showing hold-up or midfield styles, the early leaders will have breathing space to establish a rhythm before facing challenges. This pace setup strongly favors prominent runners and those who can race handily rather than get buried in traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Early Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Shirakawa or another prominent runner gets an easy time in front with soft fractions
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the pace-setter to kick clear when challenged, while hold-up horses struggle to make up ground from the back of a large field. Those racing closer to the pace have first run on the field when the sprint develops.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Problems Late
scenarios.trigger: If the large field bunches up turning for home with multiple hold-up horses looking for gaps
scenarios.body: Several fancied runners get checked or have to switch wide, allowing a horse with a clear run or one that's been prominent throughout to capitalize. The pace may collapse but positioning proves more important than raw finishing speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Shirakawa sets a genuine pace and Emerald Coast or Mali Star press the leader from early
scenarios.body: The honest pace stretches the field and allows the best stayers to come through, with those racing handy having the tactical advantage. Late closers get their chance but need to be good enough to reel in horses that have had perfect trips.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If no horse wants the lead and they crawl through the early stages
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 3f pole with the entire field still in contention, suiting horses with the best turn of foot regardless of their usual style. Hold-up horses finally get the scenario they need but must have genuine class to capitalize.

watchPoints.text: Shirakawa and Elora Prince could get too easy a lead if other prominent runners fail to go forward early
Traffic problems are highly likely given 11 hold-up horses in a 14-runner field on Bath's tight track
Us Officer's return from 276-day absence with new headgear makes him hard to assess
Mali Star and Atalanta Mist both have strong course form but need to overcome their hold-up styles
Multiple horses making debuts for new trainers including Elora Prince and New Objective add uncertainty

races.paceDynamic: Man Is King is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start, likely setting a measured pace without pressure given most rivals prefer hold-up tactics. With eight of ten runners showing hold-up tendencies (Revich, Nuptown Girl, Four Fifty, City Escape, Crimson Road, Galactic Glow, Moonlit Cloud, Bobby Dassler), only Douglas Dc offers any early support in a prominent role. The lack of early pace will create a tactical affair with a bunched field turning for home, setting up a sprint finish over the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Man Is King Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Man Is King gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: He dictates ideal fractions and has first run on the field, with Douglas Dc best placed to respond from his prominent position. The hold-up horses get caught in traffic and can't mount effective challenges.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes even slower than expected and all hold-up horses get clear runs
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint with Moonlit Cloud and Galactic Glow using their Bath course experience to navigate the finish. Man Is King gets swamped by superior finishing speed in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses get blocked and only a few find clear passages
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with Nuptown Girl and Four Fifty benefiting from superior jockey partnerships (Hornby/Queally) to find racing room. Course specialists like Galactic Glow suffer in the melee despite their local knowledge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Pace Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Douglas Dc or another runner challenges Man Is King early and forces stronger fractions
scenarios.body: The increased tempo plays into the hands of proven stayers like Crimson Road and Bobby Dassler who have recent 1m2f+ form. Man Is King gets pressured off his ideal tactics and fades in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Man Is King breaking smartly and getting an uncontested lead could prove decisive given the lack of early pace pressure
Douglas Dc's early positioning will determine if Man Is King faces any pressure or gets a completely solo lead
Hold-up horses Galactic Glow and Moonlit Cloud drawing wide may struggle to get competitive positions from their preferred tactics
Jockey bookings of Rob Hornby on Nuptown Girl and Tom Queally on Four Fifty suggest market confidence despite concerning form profiles
Going remains good across all distances at Bath which may disadvantage Galactic Glow whose wins came on softer surfaces
